sections.title: Detailed Brief Overview
rows: **Acids, Bases & Salts** (अम्ल, क्षार एवं लवण) for UPSSSC PET General Science.
Chemical compounds classified by their ion behavior, taste, and reaction with indicators.
Defined by **Arrhenius**, **Bronsted-Lowry**, and **Lewis** theories over the 19th and 20th centuries.
Forms the foundation of chemistry questions in UPSSSC PET, covering daily life applications and reactions.
Acids are sour and turn blue litmus red; Bases are bitter, soapy, and turn red litmus blue.
Ranges from **0 to 14**, where **7** is neutral, below 7 is acidic, and above 7 is basic.
Frequently tested via direct MCQs on natural sources of acids, pH values, and neutralization reactions.

items.title: 1. Definition and Concepts of Acids and Bases
items.content:
• **Arrhenius Theory:** Acids release **Hydrogen ions (H⁺)** in water; Bases release **Hydroxide ions (OH⁻)** in water.
• **Bronsted-Lowry Theory:** Acids are **proton donors**; Bases are **proton acceptors**.
• **Lewis Theory:** Acids are **electron-pair acceptors**; Bases are **electron-pair donors**.
• **Mnemonic for Litmus Paper:** **ANIL** (Acid turns Blue to Red) and **BASE** (Base turns Red to Blue).

items.title: 2. Natural Sources of Organic Acids
items.content:
• **Acetic Acid:** Found in **Vinegar** (सिरका).
• **Citric Acid:** Found in **Lemon** and **Oranges** (नींबू, संतरा).
• **Lactic Acid:** Found in **Sour Milk / Curd** (दही).
• **Formic Acid (Methanoic Acid):** Found in **Ant sting** and **Nettle leaf** (चींटी का डंक).
• **Malic Acid:** Found in **Apple** (सेब).
• **Tartaric Acid:** Found in **Tamarind** (इमली).
• **Oxalic Acid:** Found in **Tomato** (टमाटर).

items.title: 3. The pH Scale and Indicators
items.content:
• **pH Scale:** Introduced by **Sorenson** in **1909** to measure hydrogen ion concentration.
• **Indicators:** Substances that change color in acidic or basic mediums.
• **Natural Indicators:** **Litmus** (from lichen), **Turmeric** (हल्दी), **Red Cabbage**.
• **Synthetic Indicators:** **Phenolphthalein** (Colorless in acid, pink in base), **Methyl Orange** (Red in acid, yellow in base).
• **Mnemonic for pH Range:** **A**cids are **7** and below, **B**ases are **7** to **14** (**A** comes before **B**, Acid before Base on the scale).

items.title: 4. Strong vs Weak Acids and Bases
items.content:
• **Strong Acids:** Completely dissociate in water (e.g., **Hydrochloric Acid [HCl]**, **Sulphuric Acid [H₂SO₄]**, **Nitric Acid [HNO₃]**).
• **Weak Acids:** Partially dissociate in water (e.g., **Acetic Acid [CH₃COOH]**, **Citric Acid**).
• **Strong Bases:** Completely dissociate in water (e.g., **Sodium Hydroxide [NaOH]**, **Potassium Hydroxide [KOH]**).
• **Weak Bases:** Partially dissociate in water (e.g., **Ammonium Hydroxide [NH₄OH]**).

items.title: 5. Salts and Their Types
items.content:
• **Neutral Salt:** Formed by strong acid + strong base (e.g., **NaCl**, pH = 7).
• **Acidic Salt:** Formed by strong acid + weak base (e.g., **NH₄Cl**, pH < 7).
• **Basic Salt:** Formed by weak acid + strong base (e.g., **Na₂CO₃**, pH > 7).
• **Water of Crystallization:** Fixed number of water molecules in one formula unit of a salt (e.g., **CuSO₄·5H₂O** is blue, **Na₂CO₃·10H₂O** is washing soda).

sections.title: Comprehensive Data Tables
rows: Found in human stomach for digestion; used in industry.
Known as **King of Chemicals**; used in car batteries.
Caustic soda; used in soap making and paper industry.
Washing Soda; used for softening hard water.
Baking Soda; used in fire extinguishers and cooking.
Bleaching Powder; used for water disinfection.
Plaster of Paris; used for setting fractured bones.
Highly acidic environment for protein digestion.

items.definition: **A**cid **N**il **I**ndicates **L**itmus transformation: **A**cid turns **B**lue to **R**ed. Remember **ANIL** = **A**cid turns **B**lue into **R**ed (Wait, use **ABR**: **A**cid **B**lue **R**ed -> ABR format).
Sulphuric acid (**H₂SO₄**) is the **King of Chemicals** because it is used in maximum industrial manufacturing processes and batteries.
Baking soda has **Hydrogen** (**NaHCO₃** - contains 'Bi' meaning two parts or H), while Washing Soda has **10 water molecules** (**Na₂CO₃·10H₂O**).
Plaster of Paris has **half** a molecule of water (**½H₂O**), whereas Gypsum has **two** molecules of water (**2H₂O**). Remember: Gypsum is full (2), Plaster is half (1/2).
Ant sting contains **Formic Acid** (also called **Methanoic Acid**). Relief is given by rubbing a mild base like **Baking Soda** or **Soap**.
Remember **Sorenson** invented the pH scale in **1909**. Think of 'Sore' throat needing pH balance.

items.term: Mistake 1: Confusing Acid and Base Litmus Colors
items.definition: Students often invert blue and red. Remember: Acids are aggressive like fire (**Red**), so they turn blue litmus **red**.

items.term: Mistake 2: Water of Crystallization in Plaster of Paris
items.definition: Confusing Plaster of Paris formula (**CaSO₄·½H₂O**) with Gypsum (**CaSO₄·2H₂O**). Always check the water coefficient.
Thinking higher pH means higher acidity. Remember: pH **0-6** is acidic, **7** is neutral, and **8-14** is basic (acidity increases as pH decreases).

items.term: Mistake 4: Chemical Name of Baking Soda
items.definition: Confusing Sodium Bicarbonate (**NaHCO₃**) with Sodium Carbonate (**Na₂CO₃**). Bicarbonate has hydrogen and is used in baking.
Forgetting that Tamarind contains **Tartaric acid**, while Tomato contains **Oxalic acid**. Do not mix up citrus fruits (citric acid) with apples (malic acid).
Acids are substances that taste sour and release **H⁺ ions** in aqueous solution.
Bases are substances that taste bitter, feel soapy, and release **OH⁻ ions** in aqueous solution.
Reaction between an acid and a base to form **salt and water** (e.g., HCl + NaOH → NaCl + H₂O).
The pH scale ranges from **0 to 14**, measuring hydrogen ion activity.
Phenolphthalein remains **colorless in acidic** medium and turns **pink in basic** medium.
Chemical formula for bleaching powder is **CaOCl₂** (Calcium oxychloride).
Rainwater with a pH of less than **5.6** is termed **Acid Rain**.
Tooth decay starts when mouth pH falls below **5.5** due to acid production by bacteria.
Bee stings inject an acid; application of mild base like **baking soda** provides relief.
Electrolysis of brine (NaCl solution) produces **Chlorine gas**, **Hydrogen gas**, and **Sodium Hydroxide**.

upscNotes.content: UPSSSC PET frequently asks direct match-the-following questions on natural sources of acids and chemical formulas of commercial salts. Memorize the tables thoroughly.
A common trap in exam questions is asking for the chemical name of Plaster of Paris vs Gypsum based on fraction vs whole number of water molecules. Pay close attention to subscripts.
Remember that pH is a logarithmic scale. A decrease of 1 unit in pH represents a tenfold increase in hydrogen ion concentration.
Do not confuse washing soda (**Na₂CO₃·10H₂O**) with baking soda (**NaHCO₃**). Questions often test the exact number of water molecules of crystallization.

keyTakeaways: Acids turn blue litmus red; Bases turn red litmus blue.
The pH scale ranges from 0 (strong acid) to 14 (strong base), with 7 being neutral.
Sulphuric acid (H₂SO₄) is known as the King of Chemicals.
Neutralization reactions always yield salt and water.
Plaster of Paris formula is CaSO₄·½H₂O, derived by heating Gypsum.
Common salt (NaCl) is a neutral salt formed by strong acid and strong base.
